question: Does mu_G have a zero outside spec(T_G) for a (3,4)-biregular graph G?
why_this_class: Degrees in {3,4} satisfy delta >= 3 and Delta <= 2*delta-2, so by DegreeBound.lean the
universal cover has no nonzero point spectrum. The Aomoto escape, which invalidated every
previous attack on Conjecture D3, is machine-checked to be unavailable here. A root outside
the bands would therefore be an unconditional counterexample to Conjecture 10, needing no
The (3,4)-biregular tree is also the only member of the trap-free class with a spectral gap:
random mixed {3,4} graphs have continuous spectrum down through the origin.

windows_tested.note: Both windows are tested. Heilmann-Lieb only gives |x| < 2*sqrt3 = 3.4641 > 3.1463, so the upper window is not empty a priori and cannot be assumed away.

method.matching_counts: subset DP over the size-3t side of the bipartition, exact in i128
method.polynomial: mu_G = x^(n-2nu) Q(x^2), Q hyperbolic with all roots real and strictly positive
method.root_count: Budan-Fourier on Q, evaluated in exact BigInt rational arithmetic
method.why_budan_fourier: for a hyperbolic polynomial the Budan-Fourier count is exact, not an upper bound with even defect, and it needs no polynomial remainder sequence, so no Sturm coefficient blowup
method.per_graph_consistency_check: V(0) = deg Q must hold; a graph failing it is counted, not silently accepted

verdict: P80 holds on this sweep. No zero of mu_G outside spec(T_G) anywhere in the sample.
caveats: This is a sample, not a proof. Coverage is t <= 6, i.e. n <= 42, and it is exhaustive only at t = 1 and t = 2. The run ended because the t range was exhausted, not because the time budget was reached.
Random graphs are drawn by stub pairing with multi-edge rejection, which does not sample connected (3,4)-biregular graphs uniformly.
The verdicts are exact. The COVERAGE is what is uncertain, which is the opposite of the situation in the cavity-classifier searches elsewhere in this repository.
A negative result. It is evidence for Conjecture 10 in the trap-free class, and it removes the most plausible place a counterexample could have hidden.
